issues.failure_explanation: Bochner L_2 elements are equivalence classes, so point values v(y_i) at arbitrary sample points are not well-defined. The RKHS finite-trace assumption only gives point evaluations on a full-measure set, not for arbitrary y_i and not for general L_2 functions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict sample points to a full-measure set where K(y,y)<infty (or otherwise choose admissible pointwise representatives) and define the sampling operators on that admissible class.
issues.overall_effect: Every point-sampling algorithm and theorem that invokes S_k, S_n^X, or S_{cn}^X is unsupported until point evaluations are made well-defined on the sampled set.
issues.title: Sampling operator uses undefined point values in L_2
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis restores well-definedness without changing the rates or the main method.

issues.failure_explanation: Since {phi_s} is orthonormal and K(x,y)=sum_s sigma_s^{-2} phi_s(x) overline{phi_s(y)}, the eigenvalues of the kernel are sigma_s^{-2}, not sigma_s^{-1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated eigenvalues sigma_s^{-1} by sigma_s^{-2}.
issues.overall_effect: A standalone description of the RKHS is false, though it is not used in the subsequent estimates.
issues.title: RKHS eigenvalues misstated
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and does not affect the stated recovery rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The least squares approximation can be computed using the Moore-Penrose inverse

issues.failure_explanation: The text says the solution uses the Moore-Penrose inverse, but the displayed formula uses an ordinary inverse. If L^* W L is singular, the algorithm is not well-defined as written. The displayed weight matrix also has only n entries instead of cn.

failure_location.quote: (\boldsymbol L^\ast\boldsymbol W\boldsymbol L)^{-1}\boldsymbol L^\ast\boldsymbol W (f(\by_1), \dots, f(\by_{cn}))^{\top}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse (L^* W L)^+ and define W with cn diagonal entries.
issues.overall_effect: The stated least-squares algorithm is not a well-defined executable procedure in all cases needed by the downstream convergence theorems.
issues.title: Least-squares formula uses inverse instead of Moore-Penrose inverse
issues.why_classification: Replacing the inverse by the pseudoinverse is a standard local repair and does not change the advertised rates on full-rank events.

issues.failure_explanation: In Assumption (i) the least-squares subspace has dimension m=floor(n/(20 log n)). The stated bound in Theorem (i) uses the tail starting at n/log n, which is 20 times larger. The cited scalar result and the construction support a tail from m (or a comparable constant multiple), not from n/log n. For arbitrary decreasing d_s this makes the stated inequality unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace n/log n by m, or by a fixed constant multiple of n/log n, or insert the corresponding universal constant.
issues.overall_effect: The exact random least-squares guarantee in part (i) and the rate consequences built from it are not supported as stated.
issues.title: Random least-squares bound uses the wrong truncation index
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and the advertised (n/log n)^{-1/q} rate survives under the standard tail estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: The set B_{X,sigma}^q(M,N) is defined only by the H_{X,sigma} norm bound M; N is a bound on the weight sequence sigma, not a factor scaling the function class. The displayed equality with an MN factor is false. The proof also replaces the actual tail sum by an unrelated asymptotic expression k^{-2/q} without deriving it from ||sigma^{-1}||_q<=N.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove sup over B^q(M,N) <= M sup over the unit H-ball, then bound the tail sums of sigma_s^{-2} using ||sigma^{-1}||_q<=N, and repair the malformed display.
issues.overall_effect: The central convergence-rate theorem for the weighted balls is not proved, and the later tensor-product, PDE, and holomorphic applications that cite it lose their source-supported proof.
issues.title: Proof of the Bochner rate theorem incorrectly factors out N
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement is plausible and can be salvaged by a contained but nontrivial estimate; nevertheless the given proof is invalid and the central result is currently unsupported.

issues.failure_explanation: The lower bound is claimed for arbitrary N, but the proposed test sequence sigma_s=s^{1/q}(log(s+1))^eps has a fixed ell_q norm, not the parameter N. The missing N-scaling of sigma and the needed lower estimate for d_n(B^q) are not provided, so the displayed quasi-optimality relation is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Scale the test weight sequence so that ||sigma^{-1}||_q=N and prove the Kolmogorov-width lower bound d_n(B^q) approximately M N n^{-1/q}(log n)^{-eps}.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised quasi-optimality of the convergence rate is not established.
issues.title: Quasi-optimality lower bound is not proved for arbitrary N
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained but requires a nontrivial lower-bound argument; the quasi-optimality claim does not follow from the source as written.

issues.failure_explanation: For a countably infinite index set, a positive sequence in ell_q must tend to 0, so its reciprocal tends to infinity and cannot belong to ell_q. The hypothesis sigma in ell_q and sigma^{-1} in ell_q is inconsistent.

failure_location.quote: For a set  $\bsigma=(\sigma_\bs)_{\bs \in \FF}\in\ell_q(\NN)$ of positive numbers such that $\norm{\bsigma^{-1}}{\ell_q(\NN)} \le N$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the erroneous condition sigma in ell_q or replace it by the intended condition on sigma^{-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of the tensor-product weighted balls used in the applications is based on an impossible class of weights.
issues.title: Tensor-product weight condition is impossible
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local premise repair; the rest of the framework already uses sigma^{-1} in ell_q.

issues.failure_explanation: The weighted ell_2 condition gives (sigma_b ||v_b||) in ell_2 and sigma^{-1} in ell_q with q<2. This implies unconditional L_2 convergence, but not absolute convergence of the unweighted series unless an additional summability condition such as sigma^{-1} in ell_1 is imposed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace "absolutely and unconditionally" by "unconditionally in L_2" or add a hypothesis ensuring sigma^{-1} in ell_1.
issues.overall_effect: The prose claim about absolute convergence of the GPC expansion is false as stated for general 1<=q<2.
issues.title: Absolute convergence of the GPC series is overclaimed
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and does not affect the sampling recovery rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma does not define v, does not state that M and N exist, and gives only a finiteness condition rather than the needed smallness condition for lognormal analyticity. The displayed formula for sigma_b uses the undefined index s_j' and is not shown to yield ||sigma^{-1}||_q<=N.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define v as the PDE solution, state the existence of M and N, give a correct sigma_b, and add the missing smallness/analyticity hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The lognormal PDE application has no valid weighted summability input, so the lognormal part of the PDE convergence theorem is unsupported.
issues.title: Lognormal summability lemma is ill-posed
issues.why_classification: The lemma is central to the lognormal PDE result and the source does not contain a corrected, usable statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma does not define v or state that M and N exist. The constants c_{s_j}^{a,b} are undefined. Moreover, the weighted smallness assumption does not by itself guarantee uniform ellipticity of a(y) for all y in [-1,1]^infinity unless an additional condition relating rho_j and the coefficients is imposed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define v as the PDE solution, state the existence of M and N, define the constants c_{s_j}^{a,b}, and add a uniform ellipticity hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The affine PDE application lacks a well-defined summability and ellipticity input, so the affine part of the PDE convergence theorem is unsupported.
issues.title: Affine summability lemma is ill-posed
issues.why_classification: The lemma is central to the affine PDE result and the source does not contain a corrected, usable statement.

The parameter N is never introduced, and the displayed definition of rho_j is not integrated with the admissibility condition or the claimed summability estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define sigma_b explicitly for the holomorphic GPC setting, introduce N, and correct the rho_j hypothesis.
